details:
Project Name: ORBIT – Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer

1. What does your project do or how does it work?

ORBIT is an interactive, 3D space exploration and astronaut training platform designed for students aged 14–15. It makes learning about space fun through games, simulations, challenges, and interactive educational activities.

The platform allows students to experience the journey of becoming a junior astronaut through seven progressive training phases, including Astronaut Training, Rocket Engineering, Space Navigation, Planet Exploration, Spacecraft Operations, Emergency Mission Training, and a Final Space Mission.

Users can explore an interactive 3D solar system, discover information about different planets, learn about spacecraft, and participate in educational space missions.

A friendly robot assistant named ORBIT guides students throughout their journey by explaining scientific concepts, providing hints, and helping them complete challenges.

The platform also includes a search feature, text-to-speech functionality, quizzes, achievements, and progress tracking.

2. What benefits does it have?

ORBIT makes complex space science concepts easier to understand through interactive learning.

Its main benefits include:

- Makes astronomy and space science interesting and accessible.

- Encourages curiosity about planets, satellites, rockets, and space exploration.

- Provides hands-on learning through interactive simulations.

- Develops problem-solving and critical-thinking skills.

- Helps students understand scientific concepts through practical activities.

- Encourages independent learning through challenges and quizzes.

- Makes educational content more accessible through read-aloud functionality.

- Motivates students through achievements, rewards, and progressive levels.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

Our main goal is to inspire the next generation of space explorers, scientists, and engineers.

Many students find space science difficult because they learn mainly through textbooks and theoretical explanations.

ORBIT aims to bridge this gap by transforming space education into an engaging and interactive experience.

We want students to develop an interest in astronomy, understand the science behind space missions, and become more curious about the universe.

The project also aims to make quality space education more engaging and accessible to young learners, regardless of their previous knowledge of astronomy.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

Our planned technology stack includes:

Programming Languages:

- HTML5

- CSS3

- JavaScript

- TypeScript

Frameworks and Libraries:

- React

- Tailwind CSS

- Three.js

- React Three Fiber

Development Tools:

- Visual Studio Code

- Bolt.new

- Git and GitHub

Other Technologies:

- Browser LocalStorage for saving learning progress.

- Web Speech API for text-to-speech functionality.

- NASA open educational resources and scientific datasets for space-related information.

Hardware:

- Laptop or desktop computer.

- Standard web browser.

The platform is designed to run without requiring specialized hardware.

5. How is your project creative?

ORBIT combines space education, gaming, and interactive 3D technology into one learning experience.

Instead of simply reading about planets and astronauts, students become active participants in their own space exploration journey.

Some creative elements include:

- An interactive 3D solar system where students can explore planets.

- Seven astronaut training phases that progressively introduce space science.

- A friendly robot companion that guides students.

- Interactive mission simulations and space challenges.

- Gamification through XP points, stars, badges, and achievements.

- Planet exploration pages with scientific information.

- Voice-based reading support for educational content.

The combination of 3D visualization, educational gaming, and guided astronaut training makes ORBIT an engaging approach to learning space science.

6. What factors did your team consider?

While designing ORBIT, our team considered several important factors:

Target Audience: The platform is designed specifically for students aged 14–15, so the content and activities must be simple, engaging, and age-appropriate.

Scientific Accuracy: Space-related information should be based on reliable scientific sources, including NASA resources.

Accessibility: The platform should be easy to use, with readable content, simple navigation, and text-to-speech support.

User Experience: We focused on colourful visuals, interactive elements, smooth navigation, and easy-to-understand instructions.

Technical Feasibility: As a two-member beginner-level development team, we selected technologies that are practical to develop and maintain.

Performance: The application should work smoothly on ordinary laptops and common web browsers.

Educational Value: Every game feature should support learning rather than being included only for entertainment.

Scalability: The platform should allow additional planets, missions, training activities, and educational features to be added in the future.

Conclusion

ORBIT is more than an educational website. It is an interactive space learning adventure that gives young students an opportunity to explore the universe, understand space science, and experience the excitement of astronaut training.

Our vision is to make space education more engaging, accessible, and inspiring for the next generation.
